source.text: Τότε προσέρχονται τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων Φαρισαῖοι καὶ γραμματεῖς λέγοντες Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταί σου παραβαίνουσιν τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων;

records.literal_gloss: Then come to the Jesus from Jerusalem Pharisees and scribes saying, \v 2 Because of what the disciples of you break the tradition of the elders?

en.L: Then Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem come to Jesus, saying, \v 2 "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples break the tradition of the elders?
en.B: Then Pharisees and scribes arrived from Jerusalem and put a question to Jesus: \v 2 "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples go against the tradition handed down by the elders?
en.R: Then some Pharisees and teachers of the law came from Jerusalem to see Jesus. They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 2 "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers break the rules that our leaders of long ago handed down?

es.L: Entonces se acercan a Jesús, desde Jerusalén, fariseos y escribas, diciendo: \v 2 «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos quebrantan la tradición de los ancianos?
es.B: Entonces unos fariseos y escribas llegaron de Jerusalén y le hicieron a Jesús esta pregunta: \v 2 «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos van en contra de la tradición transmitida por los ancianos?
es.R: Entonces unos fariseos y unos maestros de la ley vinieron desde Jerusalén para ver a Jesús. Le preguntaron: \v 2 «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} seguidores desobedecen las reglas que nos dejaron nuestros líderes de hace mucho tiempo?

fr.L: Alors des Pharisiens et des scribes venus de Jérusalem s’approchent de Jésus, disant : \v 2 « Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples transgressent-ils la tradition des anciens ?
fr.B: Alors des Pharisiens et des scribes arrivèrent de Jérusalem et posèrent une question à Jésus : \v 2 « Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples vont-ils contre la tradition transmise par les anciens ?
fr.R: Alors des Pharisiens et des spécialistes de la Loi sont venus de Jérusalem pour voir Jésus. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé : \v 2 « Pourquoi est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples désobéissent aux règles que nos maîtres d’autrefois nous ont transmises ?

sw.L: Kisha Mafarisayo na waandishi kutoka Yerusalemu wanamjia Yesu, wakisema, \v 2 "Kwa nini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wanavunja mapokeo ya wazee?
sw.B: Kisha Mafarisayo na waandishi walifika kutoka Yerusalemu, wakamwuliza Yesu, \v 2 "Kwa nini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wanakwenda kinyume na mapokeo tuliyoachiwa na wazee?
sw.R: Kisha Mafarisayo kadhaa na walimu wa sheria walikuja kutoka Yerusalemu kumwona Yesu. Wakamwuliza, \v 2 "Kwa nini wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wanavunja kanuni ambazo viongozi wetu wa zamani walituachia?

vi.L: Bấy giờ có những người Pha-ri-si và các thầy thông giáo từ Giê-ru-sa-lem đến với Đức Giê-xu, nói rằng: \v 2 "Tại sao các môn đồ của Thầy vi phạm truyền thống của các trưởng lão?
vi.B: Bấy giờ có mấy người Pha-ri-si và thầy thông giáo từ Giê-ru-sa-lem đến hỏi Đức Giê-xu: \v 2 "Tại sao môn đồ của Thầy làm trái truyền thống của các trưởng lão?
vi.R: Lúc ấy có mấy người Pha-ri-si và thầy dạy luật từ Giê-ru-sa-lem đến gặp Đức Giê-xu. Họ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: \v 2 "Tại sao môn đồ của Thầy không giữ những luật lệ do các bậc thầy đời xưa truyền lại?

ko.L: 그때에 예루살렘에서 바리새파 사람들과 율법학자들이 예수께 와서 말한다. \v 2 "어찌하여 당신의 제자들은 장로들의 전통을 어깁니까?
ko.B: 그때에 바리새파 사람들과 율법학자들이 예루살렘에서 예수께 와서 물었다. \v 2 "왜 당신의 제자들은 장로들이 물려준 전통을 어깁니까?
ko.R: 그때 바리새파 사람들과 율법 선생 몇 사람이 예루살렘에서 예수를 찾아와 물었다. \v 2 "왜 당신의 제자들은 옛 지도자들이 물려준 규칙을 어깁니까?

pt.L: Então vêm a Jesus, de Jerusalém, fariseus e escribas, dizendo: \v 2 "Por que os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} discípulos transgridem a tradição dos anciãos?
pt.B: Então chegaram de Jerusalém alguns fariseus e escribas e fizeram uma pergunta a Jesus: \v 2 "Por que os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} discípulos desobedecem à tradição transmitida pelos anciãos?
pt.R: Então alguns fariseus e mestres da Lei vieram de Jerusalém para ver Jesus. Eles {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} perguntaram: \v 2 "Por que os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} seguidores não cumprem as regras que os nossos líderes do passado nos deixaram?

decisions.choice: the tradition of the elders: teaching handed down by earlier teachers alongside the written law
decisions.reason: The Pharisees kept rules passed on from teacher to student that applied the law to daily life. Mark 7:3-4 describes some of them. They were not part of the written law.

decisions.choice: from Jerusalem: from the center of Jewish leadership
decisions.reason: These questioners have come a long way from the city of the temple and the high council. Their coming shows that Jesus's work is now watched from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: break: step over, fail to keep
decisions.reason: The verb means to go beyond a line. The same verb is used in Jesus's reply (15:3).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: go against (B), break (R), the same word at 15:2 and 15:3
alternatives: different words in the two verses
decisions.reason: Jesus answers with the verb of their own question. Each level keeps one word for both verses so the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: teachers of the law; our leaders of long ago
decisions.reason: Readable says who the scribes were and that the elders here are teachers of earlier generations, not the town elders of the day.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (se acercan); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (llegaron, vinieron)
decisions.reason: Matthew often tells a past event in the present. Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same through the passage (verse 12).

decisions.choice: escribas (L, B); maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "escribas" names the group at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what they did, as the English "teachers of the law" does.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("s’approchent", 15:12 "disent")
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers now meet stories. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level. Literal keeps the present where Matthew tells a past event in the present, as English Literal does.

decisions.choice: les Pharisiens; les scribes (L, B), les spécialistes de la Loi (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's terms for the Gospels, as in Mark 7:1; Readable follows the English "teachers of the law".

decisions.choice: les disciples at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: English Readable says "followers"; French "disciple" is a common, transparent word, and the style guide keeps "les disciples" at every level, as in Mark's French. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (wanamjia); past at Balanced and Readable (walifika, walikuja)
decisions.reason: Matthew often tells a past event in the present. Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow. The same through the passage (verse 12).

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "waandishi" names the group at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what they did, as the English "teachers of the law" does.

decisions.choice: "truyền thống của các trưởng lão" (L, B); "những luật lệ do các bậc thầy đời xưa truyền lại" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of the parallel, Mark 7:5, with "các thầy thông giáo" (L, B) and "các thầy dạy luật" (R) for the scribes as settled for the Gospels.

decisions.choice: "Thầy" for "your" in the Pharisees' question, with no deity_pronoun span; "come" (L) with no "đã"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 7:5 and Matthew 12:38: the questioners address Jesus as a teacher, a noun of address that takes no setting span. Literal keeps Matthew's present "come" by leaving out the past marker.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 15:1-20; the Pharisees and scribes question Jesus in 합쇼체 but call him "당신"; present "말한다" (L)
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so respect for Jesus is carried by -시- and 께서 (style guide, sections 4 and 7). The scene is hostile, so, as in the parallel Mark 7:5, they speak formally but keep their distance with "당신". Literal keeps Matthew's present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: "어기다" for break, here and in 15:3; "장로들의 전통" (L, B), "옛 지도자들이 물려준 규칙" (R); "율법학자들" (L, B), "율법 선생" (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus throws their verb back at them in 15:3, so Korean keeps one verb for both. "장로들의 전통" is the form of the Korean Mark 7:3-5; Readable says what the tradition was. The scribes are worded as in the Korean Matthew 8:19 and 12:38.

decisions.choice: os teus discípulos
decisions.reason: Jesus's opponents also address him with "tu" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); the hostile tone is carried by their words, not by the form of address.

decisions.choice: transgridem (L); desobedecem a (B); não cumprem (R), the same verb in 15:2 and 15:3
decisions.reason: As the English decision: each level uses one verb for the Pharisees' question and Jesus's answer, so the echo is heard. "Transgredir" is the Literal word for stepping over a line; Balanced says "desobedecer", Readable the plainest "não cumprir".

source.text: οὐ γὰρ νίπτονται τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν ὅταν ἄρτον ἐσθίωσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Not for they wash the hands of them when bread they eat.

en.L: For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread."
en.B: They eat their meals without first washing their hands."
en.R: They do not wash their hands in the special way before they eat."

es.L: Porque no se lavan las manos cuando comen pan».
es.B: Comen sin lavarse antes las manos».
es.R: No se lavan las manos de la manera especial antes de comer».

fr.L: Car ils ne se lavent pas les mains quand ils mangent du pain. »
fr.B: Ils prennent leurs repas sans s’être d’abord lavé les mains. »
fr.R: Ils ne se lavent pas les mains selon le rite avant de manger. »

sw.L: Kwa kuwa hawanawi mikono yao wanapokula mkate."
sw.B: Wanakula chakula bila kunawa mikono kwanza."
sw.R: Hawanawi mikono yao kwa njia ile maalum kabla ya kula."

vi.L: Vì họ không rửa tay khi ăn bánh."
vi.B: Họ ăn mà không rửa tay trước."
vi.R: Họ không rửa tay theo cách thức tôn giáo đặc biệt trước khi ăn."

ko.L: 그들이 빵을 먹을 때에 손을 씻지 않기 때문입니다."
ko.B: 그들은 음식을 먹을 때 손을 씻지 않습니다."
ko.R: 그들은 음식을 먹기 전에 정해진 방식대로 손을 씻지 않습니다."

pt.L: Pois não lavam as mãos quando comem pão."
pt.B: Eles fazem as refeições sem antes lavar as mãos."
pt.R: Eles não lavam as mãos do jeito especial antes de comer."

decisions.choice: wash their hands: a washing for religious purity, not for cleanliness
decisions.reason: The law required priests to wash their hands before serving (Exodus 30:19-21). The tradition extended a ritual washing to ordinary meals (Mark 7:3). Not doing it was a matter of purity, not hygiene.

decisions.choice: eat bread: eat a meal
decisions.reason: To eat bread is a common way of saying to have a meal.

decisions.choice: in the special way
decisions.reason: Readable shows that a ritual washing is meant, not ordinary washing.

decisions.choice: "ăn bánh" (L); "ăn" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Eat bread" means to eat a meal (meaning decision); Literal keeps the Greek words, Balanced and Readable say "eat". Readable adds that the washing was a religious one, as Mark 7:2 does.

decisions.choice: "빵을 먹다" (L); "음식을 먹다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Eat bread" means eat a meal (meaning decision); Literal keeps the word "빵" (never "떡", style guide section 6), the other levels say what it means.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τί καὶ ὑμεῖς παραβαίνετε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: He but answering said to them, Because of what also you break the commandment of the God because of the tradition of you?

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said to them, "Why do you also break the commandment of God because of your tradition?
en.B: He answered them, "And why do you go against God's commandment for the sake of your tradition?
en.R: Jesus answered, "And why do you break God's command so that you can keep your own rules?

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, respondiendo, les dijo: «¿Por qué también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:quebrantan|quebrantáis}} el mandamiento de Dios por causa de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tradición?
es.B: Él les respondió: «¿Y por qué {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:van|vais}} en contra del mandamiento de Dios por causa de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tradición?
es.R: Jesús les contestó: «¿Y por qué {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:desobedecen|desobedecéis}} el mandato de Dios para poder cumplir {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} propias reglas?

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} répondit et leur dit : « Et vous, pourquoi transgressez-vous le commandement de Dieu à cause de votre tradition ?
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « Et vous, pourquoi allez-vous contre le commandement de Dieu au nom de votre tradition ?
fr.R: Jésus leur a répondu : « Et vous, pourquoi désobéissez-vous au commandement de Dieu pour pouvoir garder vos propres règles ?

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akajibu, akawaambia, "Kwa nini ninyi pia mnavunja amri ya Mungu kwa ajili ya mapokeo yenu?
sw.B: Aliwajibu, "Na ninyi, kwa nini mnakwenda kinyume na amri ya Mungu kwa ajili ya mapokeo yenu?
sw.R: Yesu aliwajibu, "Na ninyi, kwa nini mnavunja amri ya Mungu ili mshike kanuni zenu wenyewe?

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp lời và nói với họ: "Còn các người, tại sao cũng vi phạm điều răn của Đức Chúa Trời vì truyền thống của các người?
vi.B: Ngài đáp: "Còn các người, tại sao lại làm trái điều răn của Đức Chúa Trời vì truyền thống của mình?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Còn các người thì sao? Tại sao các người không giữ điều răn của Đức Chúa Trời, để giữ những luật lệ riêng của mình?

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 대답하여 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "어찌하여 너희도 너희의 전통 때문에 하나님의 계명을 어기느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "그러면 너희는 어찌하여 너희 전통을 지킨다고 하나님의 계명을 어기느냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "그러면 너희는 왜 너희 규칙을 지키려고 하나님의 명령을 어기느냐?

pt.L: Mas {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, respondendo, lhes disse: "Por que vocês também transgridem o mandamento de Deus por causa da tradição de vocês?
pt.B: Ele lhes respondeu: "E por que vocês desobedecem ao mandamento de Deus por causa da tradição de vocês?
pt.R: Jesus respondeu: "E por que vocês não cumprem o mandamento de Deus só para seguir as suas próprias regras?

decisions.choice: you also: Jesus turns their charge back on them
alternatives: you as well as my disciples
decisions.reason: They accused the disciples of breaking a tradition. Jesus asks why they themselves break a command of God, which is far more serious.

decisions.choice: your tradition: rules of human making, set against God's command
decisions.reason: In 15:2 it was "the tradition of the elders". Jesus now calls it "your tradition", their own, in contrast with what God commanded.

decisions.choice: Jesus answered
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 15:9
alternatives: closing and reopening the quotation at each sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 3-9 are one answer, so the quotation marks stay open to the end.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural "you" (ustedes|vosotros, quebrantan|quebrantáis, su|vuestra)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" (the default) and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: transgresser (L), aller contre (B), désobéir à (R), the same verb at 15:2 and 15:3
decisions.reason: As in English, Jesus answers with the verb of their own question, so each level keeps one verb for both verses and the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: "các người" for the Pharisees and scribes, through 15:3-9
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for Jesus speaking to opponents, as in Mark 7:6-13.

decisions.choice: "vi phạm" (L), "làm trái" (B), the same word as in 15:2
decisions.reason: Jesus answers with the verb of their charge (meaning decision), so each level keeps one word in 15:2 and 15:3.

decisions.choice: "계명" (L, B); "명령" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 7:8-9; Readable uses the everyday word for a command.

source.text: ὁ γὰρ θεὸς εἶπεν· Τίμα τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα, καί· Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω·

records.literal_gloss: The for God said, Honor the father and the mother, and, The [one] speaking evil of father or mother in death let him end;

en.L: For God said, 'Honor [your] father and [your] mother,' and, 'Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must surely die.'
en.B: For God said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and also, 'Anyone who reviles father or mother must be put to death.'
en.R: God said, 'Honor your father and your mother.' He also said, 'Anyone who says evil things against their father or mother must be put to death.'

es.L: Porque Dios dijo: “Honra a [tu] padre y a [tu] madre”, y: “El que hable mal del padre o de la madre, que muera sin remedio”.
es.B: Porque Dios dijo: “Honra a tu padre y a tu madre”, y también: “El que insulte a su padre o a su madre será condenado a muerte”.
es.R: Dios dijo: “Honra a tu padre y a tu madre”. También dijo: “Al que diga cosas malas contra su padre o su madre se le debe dar muerte”.

fr.L: Car Dieu a dit : “Honore ton père et ta mère”, et : “Celui qui dit du mal de père ou de mère, qu’il soit mis à mort.”
fr.B: Dieu a dit en effet : “Honore ton père et ta mère”, et aussi : “Celui qui insulte son père ou sa mère doit être mis à mort.”
fr.R: Dieu a dit : “Honore ton père et ta mère.” Il a dit aussi : “Celui qui dit du mal de son père ou de sa mère doit être puni de mort.”

sw.L: Kwa maana Mungu alisema, 'Mpe heshima baba [yako] na mama [yako],' na, 'Anayesema mabaya juu ya baba au mama, na afe kabisa.'
sw.B: Kwa maana Mungu alisema, 'Mpe heshima baba yako na mama yako,' na tena, 'Mtu anayemtukana baba yake au mama yake lazima auawe.'
sw.R: Mungu alisema, 'Waheshimu baba yako na mama yako.' Tena alisema, 'Mtu yeyote anayesema maneno mabaya dhidi ya baba yake au mama yake lazima auawe.'

vi.L: Vì Đức Chúa Trời đã phán: 'Hãy tôn kính cha mình và mẹ mình,' và: 'Kẻ nào nói xấu cha hoặc mẹ thì phải bị xử tử.'
vi.B: Vì Đức Chúa Trời đã phán: 'Hãy tôn kính cha mẹ mình,' và: 'Ai chửi rủa cha hoặc mẹ phải bị xử tử.'
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời đã phán: 'Hãy tôn kính cha mẹ mình.' Ngài cũng phán: 'Ai nói những lời độc ác xúc phạm cha hoặc mẹ mình thì phải bị xử tử.'

ko.L: 하나님께서 말씀하셨기 때문이다. '아버지와 어머니를 공경하여라.' 또 '아버지나 어머니를 악하게 말하는 사람은 반드시 죽어야 한다.'
ko.B: 하나님께서 '네 아버지와 어머니를 공경하여라' 하셨고, 또 '아버지나 어머니를 모욕하는 사람은 반드시 사형에 처해야 한다' 하셨다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 '너희 아버지와 어머니를 공경하여라' 하고 말씀하셨다. 또 '자기 아버지나 어머니를 나쁘게 말하는 사람은 사형에 처해야 한다' 하고 말씀하셨다.

pt.L: Pois Deus disse: 'Honra o pai e a mãe', e: 'Quem amaldiçoar o pai ou a mãe certamente morrerá.'
pt.B: Pois Deus disse: 'Honra o teu pai e a tua mãe', e também: 'Quem insultar o pai ou a mãe deve ser morto.'
pt.R: Deus disse: 'Honra o teu pai e a tua mãe.' E também disse: 'Quem falar mal do pai ou da mãe deve ser morto.'

decisions.choice: honor your father and your mother: Exodus 20:12; Deuteronomy 5:16
decisions.reason: The fifth commandment. Jesus calls it what God said, not only what Moses said.

decisions.choice: whoever speaks evil of father or mother: Exodus 21:17; Leviticus 20:9
decisions.reason: The law treated cursing a parent as a crime deserving death. "Let him end in death" copies a Hebrew way of speaking that stresses certainty.

decisions.choice: honor: respect, and also support and care for parents in old age
decisions.reason: Honoring parents included providing for them. This is the point of the example in 15:5-6.

decisions.choice: God said, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: God commanded, saying, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "God commanded, saying". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: reviles
decisions.reason: The verb means to speak evil of someone, to abuse with words.

decisions.choice: "Hãy tôn kính cha mình và mẹ mình" (L); "cha mẹ mình" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording of Mark 7:10: the reflexive "mình" speaks to every hearer of the commandment, where "ngươi" is archaic. "phán" because God is the speaker.

decisions.choice: "공경하다" for honor, here and in 15:6 and 15:8
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats the one verb from the commandment to his charge and to Isaiah's words; "공경하다" covers both respect and care for parents (meaning decision), and the same word keeps the repetition visible, as in the Korean Mark 7:6-10.

decisions.choice: Honra (tu)
decisions.reason: God speaking to a person uses "tu" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4), as the commandments are known in Portuguese. Literal says "o pai e a mãe", the Greek's articles, which Portuguese reads as "your" without a bracket.

decisions.choice: amaldiçoar (L); insultar (B); falar mal de (R)
decisions.reason: "Maldizer" is bookish. Literal says "amaldiçoar", the sense of the law quoted (meaning note m2); Balanced "insultar", abuse with words, as the English "reviles"; Readable the plain "falar mal".

source.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε· Ὃς ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί· Δῶρον ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς, οὐ μὴ τιμήσει τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἠκυρώσατε τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: You but say, Whoever shall say to the father or the mother, A gift whatever by me you might be profited, \v 6 not not he shall honor the father of him; and you made void the word of the God because of the tradition of you.

en.L: But you say, 'Whoever says to father or mother, "Whatever help you might have had from me [is] a gift [to God]," \v 6 {{gender:that person|he}} shall certainly not honor {{gender:their|his}} father.' And you have made void the word of God because of your tradition.
en.B: But you teach that if someone says to father or mother, 'Any support you could have received from me is set apart as a gift to God,' \v 6 then that person is excused from honoring {{gender:their|his}} father. So for the sake of your tradition you have cancelled God's word.
en.R: But you teach something else. You say people can tell their father or mother, 'I cannot help you. What I would have given you is now a gift for God.' \v 6 Then they do not have to honor their father anymore. So you make God's word mean nothing, just to keep your own rules.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: “Quien diga al padre o a la madre: ‘Cualquier ayuda que pudieras recibir de mí [es] ofrenda [a Dios]’, \v 6 de ningún modo honrará a su padre”. Y {{plural_you:han anulado|habéis anulado}} la palabra de Dios por causa de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tradición.
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:enseñan|enseñáis}} que si alguien le dice a su padre o a su madre: “Toda la ayuda que podrías recibir de mí está apartada como ofrenda para Dios”, \v 6 entonces queda libre de honrar a su padre. Así, por causa de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tradición, {{plural_you:han anulado|habéis anulado}} la palabra de Dios.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:enseñan|enseñáis}} otra cosa. {{plural_you:Dicen|Decís}} que uno puede decirle a su padre o a su madre: “No puedo ayudarte. Lo que te habría dado ahora es una ofrenda para Dios”. \v 6 Entonces ya no tiene que honrar a su padre. Así {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} que la palabra de Dios no valga nada, solo para cumplir {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} propias reglas.

fr.L: Mais vous, vous dites : si quelqu’un dit à son père ou à sa mère : “Ce dont tu aurais pu profiter de ma part [est] une offrande [à Dieu]”, \v 6 il n’honorera certainement pas son père. Et vous avez annulé la parole de Dieu à cause de votre tradition.
fr.B: Mais vous, vous enseignez que si quelqu’un dit à son père ou à sa mère : “L’aide que tu aurais pu recevoir de moi est mise à part comme offrande à Dieu”, \v 6 celui-là est dispensé d’honorer son père. Ainsi, au nom de votre tradition, vous avez aboli la parole de Dieu.
fr.R: Mais vous, vous enseignez autre chose. Vous dites qu’on peut dire à son père ou à sa mère : “Je ne peux pas t’aider. Ce que je t’aurais donné est maintenant une offrande pour Dieu.” \v 6 Après cela, on n’a plus besoin d’honorer son père. Ainsi, vous faites comme si la parole de Dieu ne comptait pas, seulement pour garder vos propres règles.

sw.L: Lakini ninyi mnasema, 'Mtu yeyote atakayemwambia baba au mama, "Msaada wowote ambao ungeupata kutoka kwangu [ni] zawadi [kwa Mungu]," \v 6 hakika hatamheshimu baba yake.' Nanyi mmelibatilisha neno la Mungu kwa ajili ya mapokeo yenu.
sw.B: Lakini ninyi mnafundisha kwamba mtu akimwambia baba yake au mama yake, 'Msaada wowote ambao ungeweza kuupata kutoka kwangu umetengwa kuwa zawadi kwa Mungu,' \v 6 basi hana tena wajibu wa kumheshimu baba yake. Hivyo kwa ajili ya mapokeo yenu mmelifuta neno la Mungu.
sw.R: Lakini ninyi mnafundisha jambo lingine. Mnasema mtu anaweza kumwambia baba yake au mama yake, 'Siwezi kukusaidia. Kile ambacho ningekupa sasa ni zawadi kwa Mungu.' \v 6 Basi hana tena haja ya kumheshimu baba yake. Kwa hiyo mnalifanya neno la Mungu lisiwe na maana yoyote, ili tu mshike kanuni zenu wenyewe.

vi.L: Nhưng các người nói: 'Ai nói với cha hoặc mẹ: "Bất cứ điều gì cha mẹ có thể được con giúp đều là của lễ [dâng cho Đức Chúa Trời]," \v 6 thì người ấy hẳn không cần tôn kính cha mình.' Như vậy các người đã làm cho lời Đức Chúa Trời ra vô hiệu vì truyền thống của các người.
vi.B: Nhưng các người dạy rằng nếu ai nói với cha hoặc mẹ: 'Những gì con có thể giúp cha mẹ đều đã dâng làm của lễ cho Đức Chúa Trời,' \v 6 thì người ấy không phải tôn kính cha mình nữa. Như thế, vì truyền thống của mình, các người đã làm cho lời Đức Chúa Trời ra vô hiệu.
vi.R: Nhưng các người lại dạy khác. Các người nói rằng một người có thể nói với cha mẹ mình: 'Con không giúp cha mẹ được. Những gì con định biếu cha mẹ, con đã dâng cho Đức Chúa Trời rồi.' \v 6 Rồi người ấy không cần phải tôn kính cha mình nữa. Như vậy, chỉ để giữ những luật lệ riêng của mình, các người làm cho lời Đức Chúa Trời trở thành vô giá trị.

ko.L: 그러나 너희는 말한다. '누구든지 아버지나 어머니에게 "제게서 받으실 수 있는 도움은 무엇이든 [하나님께 드린] 예물입니다" 하고 말하면, \v 6 그는 자기 아버지를 공경하지 않아도 된다.' 이렇게 너희는 너희의 전통 때문에 하나님의 말씀을 무효로 만들었다.
ko.B: 그러나 너희는 이렇게 가르친다. 누구든지 아버지나 어머니에게 '제가 드릴 수 있었던 도움은 무엇이든 하나님께 바친 예물입니다' 하고 말하면, \v 6 그 사람은 아버지를 공경하지 않아도 된다는 것이다. 이렇게 너희는 너희 전통을 내세워 하나님의 말씀을 헛되게 만들었다.
ko.R: 그런데 너희는 다르게 가르친다. 누구든지 아버지나 어머니에게 '저는 도와 드릴 수 없습니다. 도와 드리려던 것은 이제 하나님께 바친 예물입니다' 하고 말해도 된다고 한다. \v 6 그러면 그 사람은 더 이상 아버지를 공경하지 않아도 된다고 한다. 너희는 너희 규칙을 지키려고 하나님의 말씀을 쓸모없게 만든다.

pt.L: Mas vocês dizem: 'Quem disser ao pai ou à mãe: "Qualquer ajuda que você poderia ter de mim [é] oferta [a Deus]", \v 6 de modo nenhum honrará o seu pai.' E vocês anularam a palavra de Deus por causa da tradição de vocês.
pt.B: Mas vocês ensinam que, se alguém disser ao pai ou à mãe: 'Todo o sustento que você poderia receber de mim está separado como oferta a Deus', \v 6 essa pessoa fica dispensada de honrar o pai. Assim, por causa da tradição de vocês, vocês anularam a palavra de Deus.
pt.R: Mas vocês ensinam outra coisa. Vocês dizem que alguém pode dizer ao pai ou à mãe: 'Não posso ajudar você. O que eu daria a você agora é uma oferta para Deus.' \v 6 Aí essa pessoa não precisa mais honrar o pai. Assim vocês fazem a palavra de Deus perder o valor, só para seguir as suas próprias regras.

decisions.choice: a gift: property vowed to God, so that it could not be used for the parents
decisions.reason: Mark 7:11 gives the Hebrew word for such an offering, Corban. Vows to God were binding (Numbers 30:2). A son could declare his goods vowed to God and so put them beyond his parents' reach, while he may still have kept the use of them himself.

decisions.choice: shall not honor his father: the result of their ruling, that such a person is freed from the duty
alternatives: Jesus's own comment: such a person will certainly not honor his father
decisions.reason: The words can be the last part of the teaching Jesus reports, saying the vow releases the son from supporting his father. They can also be Jesus's comment on what follows from it. Either way, the vow ends the son's care for his parents.

decisions.choice: the word of God, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the commandment of God, the reading of many later manuscripts
the law of God, in some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts read "the word", others "the law", and many later ones "the commandment". All three point to the command of 15:4. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: his father, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: his father or his mother, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "or his mother", to match 15:4 and 15:5. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:that person|he}}; {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The rule applies to a daughter as well as a son, so the inclusive forms are the default.

decisions.choice: I cannot help you; anymore
alternatives: a gift; he shall not honor
decisions.reason: Readable says what the vow meant for the parents.

decisions.choice: cancelled (B); make mean nothing (R)
decisions.reason: The verb was used for annulling a law or a contract.

decisions.choice: quien ... su padre, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:that person|he}} and {{gender:their|his}} because English pronouns show gender. Spanish "quien" and "su padre" say "whoever" and "his or her father" without choosing, and the verb carries no pronoun, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: one level of quotation marks inside Jesus's words at Literal (“…”), with the rule they teach given as indirect speech
alternatives: a third level of quotation marks
decisions.reason: As in Mark 7:11: French marks a quotation within a quotation with “ ”, and a third level is awkward in French type. Literal reports the rule as Jesus's own statement ("vous dites : si quelqu’un dit…") and keeps the vow itself in quotation marks.

decisions.choice: no gender setting: "quelqu’un … il" (L), "celui-là" (B), "son père"
decisions.reason: English needs a setting for "that person / he" and "their / his". French "quelqu’un", "il" and "celui-là" are the ordinary generic forms and already mean a son or a daughter, and the possessive "son" agrees with "père", not with the child, so, as the style guide says, no span is added.

decisions.choice: mtu ... baba yake, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:that person|he}} and {{gender:their|his}} because English pronouns show gender. Swahili "mtu", the subject prefix a- and "yake" already mean a man or a woman, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: The son speaks to his parent as "cha mẹ" and of himself as "con"; "người ấy" and "cha mình" with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in Mark 7:11: a child speaking to father or mother says "cha mẹ" and "con". "Người ấy" and the reflexive "mình" already take in men and women, so the English gender spans have no Vietnamese counterpart.

decisions.choice: "của lễ [dâng cho Đức Chúa Trời]" (L); "đã dâng làm của lễ cho Đức Chúa Trời" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew writes the Greek word "gift" where Mark keeps the Hebrew "Corban" (Mark 7:11); Vietnamese follows Matthew and says what the gift was, property vowed to God (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: The son speaks to his parents in 합쇼체 ("제게서", "예물입니다"); "그는", "그 사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 7:11: a grown child making a formal vow to a parent uses the deferential style. Korean refers to the person without a gendered pronoun, so the English gender spans have nothing to change (style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: [하나님께 드린]
decisions.reason: The gift is property vowed to God (meaning decision); Korean "예물" alone does not say to whom, so Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: quem ... o seu pai (L); essa pessoa ... o pai (B), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs a setting to choose between "that person/their" and "he/his". Portuguese "quem" and "essa pessoa" already cover a son or a daughter, and "seu" does not mark the owner's gender, so no setting is needed (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7).

decisions.choice: oferta [a Deus] (L); oferta a Deus (B); uma oferta para Deus (R)
decisions.reason: The gift is property vowed to God (m1). "Oferta" is the Portuguese word for what is given to God; "presente" would sound like a present to a person.

source.text: ὑποκριταί, καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν περὶ ὑμῶν Ἠσαΐας λέγων·

records.literal_gloss: Hypocrites, rightly prophesied concerning you Isaiah saying,

en.L: Hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied rightly about you, saying,
en.B: You are hypocrites, and Isaiah's prophecy about you was exactly right. He said:
en.R: You hypocrites! Long ago Isaiah spoke God's message, and he described you exactly. He said,

sw.R: Ninyi wanafiki! Zamani sana Isaya alitangaza ujumbe wa Mungu, naye aliwaeleza ninyi sawasawa kabisa. Alisema,

vi.L: Hỡi những kẻ đạo đức giả, Ê-sai đã nói tiên tri đúng về các người rằng:
vi.B: Hỡi những kẻ đạo đức giả! Ê-sai đã nói tiên tri thật đúng về các người:
vi.R: Các người là những kẻ đạo đức giả! Từ xưa, Ê-sai đã truyền lại sứ điệp của Đức Chúa Trời, và ông đã nói thật đúng về các người. Ông nói:

ko.L: 위선자들아! 이사야가 너희에 대하여 잘 예언하여 말하였다.
ko.B: 너희 위선자들아! 이사야가 너희를 두고 한 예언이 참 잘 들어맞았다. 그는 이렇게 말하였다.
ko.R: 너희 위선자들아! 오래전에 이사야가 하나님의 말씀을 전했는데, 그 말이 너희에게 꼭 들어맞았다. 이사야는 이렇게 말했다.

pt.L: Hipócritas! Bem profetizou Isaías a respeito de vocês, dizendo:
pt.B: Vocês são hipócritas, e a profecia de Isaías a respeito de vocês estava certíssima. Ele disse:
pt.R: Hipócritas! Muito tempo atrás, Isaías anunciou uma mensagem de Deus e descreveu vocês direitinho. Ele disse:

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people whose religion is a performance
decisions.reason: As in 6:2. Their outward care for purity hides a heart far from God (15:8).

decisions.choice: prophesied about you: Isaiah's words to his own generation fit these leaders too
alternatives: Isaiah spoke only of people in Jesus's day
decisions.reason: Isaiah spoke to the people of Jerusalem in his own time. Jesus says the words describe his hearers just as well.

decisions.choice: spoke God's message
decisions.reason: Readable says what prophesying is.

decisions.choice: "những kẻ đạo đức giả" at every level
decisions.reason: The settled Matthew word (6:2): people whose religion is a performance (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "위선자들" at every level
decisions.reason: The settled word of the Korean Matthew and Mark 7:6; "외식하는 자" is the older church expression.

source.text: Ὁ λαὸς οὗτος τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: The people this with the lips me honors, the but heart of them far away is from me;

en.L: 'This people honors {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with [their] lips, but their heart is far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}};
en.B: 'With their lips this people honors {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but their heart keeps far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: 'These people honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with their words, but their hearts are far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: “Este pueblo con los labios {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra, pero el corazón de ellos está muy apartado de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}};
es.B: “Con los labios este pueblo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra, pero su corazón se mantiene lejos de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: “Esta gente {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra con sus palabras, pero su corazón está lejos de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

fr.L: “Ce peuple {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honore des lèvres, mais leur cœur se tient loin de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ;
fr.B: “Avec ses lèvres, ce peuple {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honore, mais son cœur reste éloigné de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: “Ces gens {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honorent par leurs paroles, mais leur cœur est loin de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: 'Watu hawa wananiheshimu kwa midomo, lakini moyo wao umekaa mbali sana {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}};
sw.B: 'Kwa midomo yao watu hawa wananipa heshima, lakini mioyo yao inakaa mbali {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}.
sw.R: 'Watu hawa wananiheshimu kwa maneno yao, lakini mioyo yao iko mbali {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}.

vi.L: 'Dân này lấy môi tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nhưng lòng họ thì xa cách {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}};
vi.B: 'Dân này tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bằng môi miệng, nhưng lòng họ thì xa cách {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: 'Dân này tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bằng lời nói, nhưng lòng họ thì ở xa {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: '이 백성은 입술로 나를 공경하지만, 그들의 마음은 나에게서 멀리 떨어져 있다.
ko.B: '이 백성은 입술로는 나를 공경하지만, 마음은 나에게서 멀리 떠나 있다.
ko.R: '이 사람들은 말로는 나를 공경하지만, 그들의 마음은 나에게서 멀리 떨어져 있다.

pt.L: 'Este povo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra com os lábios, mas o coração deles está longe de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}};
pt.B: 'Com os lábios este povo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra, mas o coração dele se mantém longe de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.
pt.R: 'Esse povo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra com palavras, mas o coração dessas pessoas está longe de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 29:13: God speaks of his people
decisions.reason: Matthew quotes in a form close to the Greek Old Testament. In Isaiah the Lord is the speaker, so "me" is God.

decisions.choice: this people honors me with their lips, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: this people draws near to me with their mouth and honors me with their lips, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "draws near to me with their mouth and", which is in the Greek of Isaiah 29:13. Early manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: heart: the inner self, where thoughts and choices begin
decisions.reason: As in 12:34. Honor in words means nothing when the heart, the person's real self, stays away from God.

decisions.choice: spans on "me" for God
decisions.reason: God speaks in Isaiah, so the pronouns for him take the deity_pronoun setting, as in 12:18.

decisions.choice: with their words
decisions.reason: Readable says what honoring with the lips means.

decisions.choice: a span on nami (from me); none on the object prefix -ni- (wananiheshimu)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: The English "me" for God takes the setting. Swahili carries the object in the prefix -ni- of the verb, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives (nami, kwangu, wako, yangu). Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: God says "Ta" in the words of Isaiah, with the deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in Mark 7:6: God is the speaker in the quotation (meaning decision), so the pronoun is the reverent "Ta" under the setting, as the English "me" is.

decisions.choice: God speaks in 해라체 with "나"; no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: God speaking uses the plain style (style guide, section 7a); Korean has no capitals for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: com os lábios, with no bracket
decisions.reason: Portuguese uses the article for a part of the body, which the Greek also has, so Literal supplies nothing where the English brackets "their".

records.literal_gloss: In vain but they worship me, teaching [as] teachings commandments of men.

en.L: and in vain they worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, teaching [as] teachings [the] commandments of {{gender:people|men}}.'"
en.B: Their worship of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is empty, for the doctrines they teach are commands made by human beings.'"
en.R: Their worship of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} means nothing. They teach rules that people made up, as if those rules came from God.'"

es.B: Vacío es el culto que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rinden, porque las doctrinas que enseñan son mandatos hechos por seres humanos”».
es.R: El culto que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dan no vale nada. Enseñan reglas que inventó la gente, como si vinieran de Dios”».

fr.R: Le culte qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rendent ne vaut rien. Ils enseignent des règles inventées par les gens, comme si elles venaient de Dieu.” »

sw.L: na wananiabudu bure, wakifundisha [kama] mafundisho amri za wanadamu.'"
sw.B: Ibada yao {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} haina maana, kwa sababu mafundisho wanayofundisha ni amri zilizotungwa na wanadamu.'"
sw.R: Ibada yao {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} si kitu. Wanafundisha kanuni zilizobuniwa na watu, kana kwamba zimetoka kwa Mungu.'"

vi.L: và họ thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cách vô ích, dạy [như] giáo lý những điều răn của loài người.'"
vi.B: Họ thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thật vô ích, vì họ lấy điều răn của loài người mà dạy như giáo lý.'"
vi.R: Họ thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chẳng ích gì. Họ dạy những luật lệ do loài người đặt ra, như thể đó là lời dạy của Đức Chúa Trời.'"

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 사람들의 계명들을 교훈으로 가르치며, 헛되이 나를 예배한다.'"
ko.B: 그들이 나를 예배해도 아무 소용이 없다. 사람이 만든 계명을 하나님의 가르침처럼 가르치기 때문이다.'"
ko.R: 그들이 나를 예배하는 것은 아무 뜻이 없다. 사람들이 지어낸 규칙을 하나님께서 주신 것처럼 가르치기 때문이다.'"

pt.L: e em vão {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} adoram, ensinando [como] doutrinas mandamentos {{gender:de seres humanos|de homens}}.'"
pt.B: A adoração que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} prestam é vazia, pois as doutrinas que ensinam são mandamentos criados por seres humanos.'"
pt.R: A adoração que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} oferecem não vale nada. Eles ensinam regras que as pessoas inventaram, como se essas regras viessem de Deus.'"

decisions.choice: in vain: to no purpose, empty
decisions.reason: Their worship achieves nothing, because God does not accept it.

decisions.choice: teaching as doctrines the commands of people: presenting human rules as God's teaching
alternatives: teaching both God's law and human rules
decisions.reason: The fault is that rules made by people are taught as if they had God's authority. That is what Jesus has shown in 15:3-6.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: as if those rules came from God
decisions.reason: Readable says what "teaching as doctrines" means here.

decisions.choice: mandamientos {{gender:humanos|de hombres}}
decisions.reason: As the English {{gender:people|men}}: the Greek word means human beings, and Spanish can say it either way. Balanced and Readable say "seres humanos" and "la gente", which need no span.

decisions.choice: "loài người" with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in Mark 7:7: "loài người" (humankind) already takes in men and women.

decisions.choice: "사람들", "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" already includes men and women (style guide, section 7), as in the Korean Mark 7:7.

records.literal_gloss: And having called to [him] the crowd he said to them, Hear and understand;

en.L: And calling the crowd to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Listen and understand:
en.B: Then Jesus called the crowd over to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Hear this, and understand it.
en.R: Then Jesus called the crowd to come near. He said, "Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and understand what I say.

es.L: Y llamando a la multitud hacia [{{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}}], les dijo: «{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} y {{plural_you:entiendan|entended}}:
es.B: Entonces Jesús llamó a la multitud para que se acercara y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}} esto, y {{plural_you:entiéndanlo|entendedlo}}.
es.R: Luego Jesús llamó a la gente para que se acercara. Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Escúchenme|Escuchadme}} y {{plural_you:entiendan|entended}} lo que digo.

fr.L: Et ayant appelé la foule à [{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Écoutez et comprenez :
fr.B: Puis Jésus appela la foule auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et dit : « Écoutez, et comprenez bien.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus a appelé la foule à s’approcher. Il a dit : « Écoutez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et comprenez ce que je dis.

sw.L: Na alipouita umati [{{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}], akawaambia, "Sikieni na mwelewe:
sw.B: Kisha Yesu aliuita umati wa watu uje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, akasema, "Sikilizeni haya, na myaelewe.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliwaita watu wa umati waje karibu. Akasema, "Nisikilizeni, na mwelewe ninachosema.

vi.L: Và gọi đoàn dân đến [với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}], {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Hãy nghe và hiểu:
vi.B: Rồi Đức Giê-xu gọi đoàn dân đến và nói: "Hãy nghe và hiểu điều này:
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu gọi đoàn dân đến gần. Ngài nói: "Mọi người hãy nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và cố gắng hiểu điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 무리를 [가까이] 불러 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "듣고 깨달아라.
ko.B: 그리고 예수께서 무리를 가까이 부르시고 말씀하셨다. "잘 듣고 깨달아라.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 예수께서 사람들을 가까이 부르셨다. 그리고 말씀하셨다. "내 말을 잘 듣고 깨달아라.

pt.L: E, chamando a multidão para junto [de {{deity_pronoun:si|Si}}], {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes disse: "Ouçam e entendam:
pt.B: Então Jesus chamou a multidão para perto de {{deity_pronoun:si|Si}} e disse: "Ouçam isto e entendam.
pt.R: Então Jesus chamou a multidão para chegar perto. Ele disse: "Escutem o que eu digo e procurem entender.

decisions.choice: calling the crowd: the teaching is for everyone, not only the leaders
alternatives: a private word to the disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus turns from the Pharisees and scribes to the whole crowd. What makes a person unclean concerns everyone.

decisions.choice: understand: grasp the meaning, not only hear the words
decisions.reason: The same verb runs through the parables of chapter 13 (13:13-15, 19, 23). Hearing is not enough without understanding.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new part of the scene begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 15:11
alternatives: closing the quotation in this sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 10-11 are one saying.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on pronouns left out or joined to the verb (se acercara, Escúchenme)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the verb, where there is nothing separate to capitalise. So the setting covers fewer words than in English: separate pronouns and possessives (él, lo, le, me, mí, tus, sus). This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "Mọi người" (R) for the crowd
decisions.reason: As in Mark 7:14: Readable addresses the crowd with the neutral "mọi người", which a plain reader hears as an invitation.

decisions.choice: Escutem o que eu digo, with no span
decisions.reason: Readable says "o que eu digo", the plain Portuguese for "listen to me"; "eu" for Jesus takes no span (section 7), so the English span on "me" has no counterpart.

records.literal_gloss: Not the entering into the mouth defiles the man, but the going out of the mouth this defiles the man.

en.L: It is not what enters into the mouth [that] defiles the {{gender:person|man}}, but what comes out of the mouth, this defiles the {{gender:person|man}}."
en.B: A person is not made unclean by what goes into the mouth. What makes a person unclean is what comes out of it."
en.R: What you put into your mouth does not make you unclean before God. It is what comes out of your mouth that makes you unclean."

es.L: No [es] lo que entra en la boca [lo que] contamina {{gender:a la persona|al hombre}}, sino que lo que sale de la boca, eso contamina {{gender:a la persona|al hombre}}».
es.B: A una persona no la hace impura lo que entra por la boca. Lo que hace impura a una persona es lo que sale de ella».
es.R: Lo que te metes en la boca no te hace impuro ante Dios. Lo que sale de tu boca es lo que te hace impuro».

fr.L: Ce n’est pas ce qui entre dans la bouche qui souille {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}, mais ce qui sort de la bouche, voilà ce qui souille {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}. »
fr.B: Ce n’est pas ce qui entre dans la bouche qui rend une personne impure. Ce qui la rend impure, c’est ce qui en sort. »
fr.R: Ce que vous mettez dans votre bouche ne vous rend pas impurs devant Dieu. Ce qui vous rend impurs, c’est ce qui sort de votre bouche. »

sw.L: Si kinachoingia kinywani kinachomfanya mtu najisi, bali kinachotoka kinywani, hicho kinamfanya mtu najisi."
sw.B: Mtu hafanywi najisi na kile kinachoingia kinywani mwake. Kinachomfanya mtu kuwa najisi ni kile kinachotoka kinywani."
sw.R: Kile unachokitia kinywani hakikufanyi najisi mbele za Mungu. Kinachokufanya najisi ni kile kinachotoka kinywani mwako."

vi.L: Không phải điều gì vào miệng làm cho con người ô uế, nhưng điều từ miệng ra, chính điều ấy làm cho con người ô uế."
vi.B: Không phải những gì vào miệng làm cho một người ô uế. Chính những gì từ miệng ra mới làm cho người ấy ô uế."
vi.R: Những gì người ta ăn vào miệng không làm cho họ ô uế trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời. Chính những gì từ miệng họ nói ra mới làm cho họ ô uế."

ko.L: 입으로 들어가는 것이 사람을 부정하게 하는 것이 아니라, 입에서 나오는 것, 이것이 사람을 부정하게 한다."
ko.B: 입으로 들어가는 것이 사람을 부정하게 하는 것이 아니다. 입에서 나오는 것이 사람을 부정하게 한다."
ko.R: 입에 넣는 음식이 너희를 하나님 앞에서 더럽게 만드는 것이 아니다. 입에서 나오는 것이 너희를 더럽게 만든다."

pt.L: Não é o que entra na boca [que] contamina o {{gender:ser humano|homem}}, mas o que sai da boca, isso contamina o {{gender:ser humano|homem}}."
pt.B: Não é o que entra pela boca que torna uma pessoa impura. O que torna uma pessoa impura é o que sai dela."
pt.R: O que você põe na boca não deixa você impuro diante de Deus. O que sai da sua boca é que deixa você impuro."

decisions.choice: defiles: makes a person unclean, unfit to come before God
decisions.reason: The verb means to make common or impure. Purity decided whether a person could take part in worship (Leviticus 11-15).

decisions.choice: what comes out of the mouth: words, and the heart they come from
decisions.reason: Jesus explains in 15:18-19 that what comes out of the mouth comes from the heart.

decisions.choice: the saying answers the question of washed hands (15:20)
alternatives: a ruling that sets aside all the food laws
decisions.reason: Matthew applies the saying to eating with unwashed hands (15:20) and does not include Mark's comment that Jesus made all foods clean (Mark 7:19). How far the saying bears on the food laws themselves is debated.

decisions.choice: the {{gender:person|man}}
decisions.reason: The word means a human being, so the inclusive form is the default. The same applies in 15:18 and 15:20.

decisions.choice: before God
decisions.reason: Readable says in whose sight a person is unclean.

decisions.choice: contaminar (L); hacer impuro (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone ritually unclean, unfit to come before God (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps one verb, "contaminar"; Balanced and Readable say "hacer impuro", which names that kind of uncleanness. The same in verses 18 and 20.

decisions.choice: {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} at Literal; "une personne" (B), "vous" (R) with no setting
decisions.reason: As in Mark 7:15: the setting goes on the noun French has to choose. "L’être humain" and "l’homme" are both masculine, so the words that refer back to them are the same under either option; Balanced and Readable are already inclusive. The same holds in 15:18 and 15:20.

decisions.choice: kumfanya mtu najisi
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone ritually unclean, unfit to come before God (meaning decision m1). "Najisi" is the word for that kind of uncleanness; "kuchafua" suggests dirt. The same in verses 18 and 20.

decisions.choice: "ô uế" for "defile", at every level and through 15:20; "con người" with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in Mark 7:15: uncleanness in the religious sense (meaning decision), not dirt. "Con người" and "người ta" already take in men and women.

decisions.choice: "người ta ăn vào miệng" ... "họ" (R)
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "you"; Vietnamese speaks of people in general with "người ta" and "họ", since a crowd is being addressed and the plain "you" would need a pronoun of relation.

decisions.choice: "부정하게 하다" (L, B); "하나님 앞에서 더럽게 만들다" (R), through 15:20; "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 7:15: the uncleanness is religious (meaning decision), which "부정" says; Readable uses the plainer "더럽게" and says it is about standing before God.

decisions.choice: contamina (L); torna impura (B); deixa impuro (R)
decisions.reason: For this passage (15:11-20). Literal keeps the vivid "contaminar"; Balanced and Readable say "impuro", the word for ritual uncleanness that kept a person from worship (m1). "Imundo" now suggests mere dirt.
